deactivate.title: The confirmation before an admin deactivates a person: what stops working, what else ends, and what stays theirs. {{first}} is the person's first name.
deactivate.description: Body under the deactivate confirmation's title. {{first}} is the person's first name.
deactivate.impactFailed: Error in the deactivate confirmation when the list of what deactivating would end can't be loaded.
deactivate.unknownError: Stands in for {{why}} in the transfer error messages when the server gave no reason. Lowercase.
deactivate.transferRefused: Error in the deactivate confirmation. {{first}} is the person's first name; {{why}} is the server's error message.
deactivate.transferLost: Error in the deactivate confirmation when the connection failed during the transfer. {{why}} is the error message; {{first}} is the person's first name.
deactivate.transferred: Toast after a transfer: {{from}} and {{to}} are people's names.
deactivate.keysSection: Accessible name of the red warning box listing the service keys (API keys) that stop working.
deactivate.keysStop: Bold start of the warning about service keys (API keys) the person made.
deactivate.keysMade: Follows the bold warning (deactivate.keysStop): the person made the keys and saw their secret values. {{first}} is their first name.
deactivate.keyNever: Muted note after a service key in the deactivate confirmation: the key was never used. Lowercase.
deactivate.keyJustNow: Muted note after a service key in the deactivate confirmation: the key was used moments ago. Lowercase.
deactivate.lastKey: Badge: this is the service account's only working key, so the account {{account}} stops working too.
deactivate.keyUsed: {{ago}} is a lowercase time phrase ("25 min ago", "yesterday").
deactivate.otherKey: Beside a service key: the service account (its name is {{account}}) has another working key, so it keeps working.
deactivate.newKey: Advice under the keys that are a service account's last: make it a new key first. {{account}} is the service account's name; a link to it follows.
deactivate.openAccount: Link to the service account in Settings › People › Service accounts. {{account}} is its name.
deactivate.alsoEnds: Heading of the list of other things deactivating ends (sessions, connected agents, scheduled tasks…), each with its outcome.
deactivate.ends.sessions: Lines of the "Also ends" list; each is followed by its outcome (deactivate.outcomes).
deactivate.ends.connectedAgents: Line of the "Also ends" list: outside AI agents (such as Claude Code) connected to the person's account.
deactivate.ends.socioGrants: Line of the "Also ends" list: access the person gave socios (AI agents) to act for them.
deactivate.ends.appSessions: Line of the "Also ends" list: open sessions of mini apps (small apps people build in Socio).
deactivate.ends.pluginAccess: Plugin sessions and the one-time codes that launch plugins.
deactivate.ends.scheduledTasks: Line of the "Also ends" list: tasks set to run at set times for the person.
deactivate.ends.jobRuns: Line of the "Also ends" list: background jobs running now for the person.
deactivate.ends.subscriptionConnections: Line of the "Also ends" list: the person's connected AI model subscriptions (their own paid plan with a model provider).
deactivate.ends.mcpConnections: Line of the "Also ends" list: connections to MCP servers (tool servers for AI agents). Keep "MCP".
deactivate.ends.roomsHandedOver: A Room is a group chat. {{first}} is the person's first name.
deactivate.ends.roomsArchived: Line of the "Also ends" list: Rooms (group chats) with no one left to run them once the person is deactivated.
deactivate.outcomes.signedOut: What happens to each line of the "Also ends" list, in a short muted phrase.
deactivate.outcomes.disconnected: Outcome beside a line of the "Also ends" list: the connection is cut. Lowercase.
deactivate.outcomes.revoked: Outcome beside a line of the "Also ends" list: the access is withdrawn. Lowercase.
deactivate.outcomes.ended: Outcome beside a line of the "Also ends" list: the sessions are closed. Lowercase.
deactivate.outcomes.paused: Outcome beside the scheduled tasks line: they are paused and kept, not deleted. Lowercase.
deactivate.outcomes.stopped: Outcome beside the job runs line: running jobs are stopped at once. Lowercase.
deactivate.outcomes.handedOver: Outcome beside the Rooms line: each Room (group chat) goes to the member who joined it first. Lowercase.
deactivate.outcomes.archived: Outcome beside the Rooms line with no one left to run them: they are archived. Lowercase.
deactivate.stays: Heading of the list of what the person owns, which stays theirs unless transferred. {{first}} is their first name.
deactivate.transfer: Button beside that heading: opens the transfer dialog to hand what they own to another person; the ellipsis says a dialog follows.
deactivate.movesTo: Beside an owned kind once a new owner is chosen: it will move to them. {{name}} is the new owner's first name. Lowercase.
deactivate.kept: Beside an owned kind when no new owner is chosen: it stays the deactivated person's. Lowercase.
deactivate.handTo: Label of the select of the person who receives everything before the deactivation.
deactivate.handToNobody: First option of the "Hand everything to" select: no one, so what they own stays theirs.
deactivate.step1: Numbered steps shown once a new owner is chosen. {{first}} is the deactivated person's first name; {{name}} is the new owner's full name.
deactivate.step2: Second numbered step. {{first}} is the deactivated person's first name.
deactivate.step3: Third numbered step. {{first}} is the deactivated person's first name.
deactivate.nothingElse: Shown in the deactivate confirmation when nothing else (keys, sessions, owned things) is affected.
deactivate.confirm: The deactivate button; the _only form when a new owner is chosen but the admin deactivates without transferring.
deactivate.transferAndDeactivate: Main button of the deactivate confirmation: transfer first, then deactivate. {{name}} is the new owner's first name.
deactivate.transferAndDeactivatePick: The same button, disabled, before a new owner is chosen; the ellipsis stands for the person still to choose.
reactivate.title: Title of the confirmation before an admin reactivates a deactivated person. {{name}} is the person's full name.
reactivate.description: Body of the reactivate confirmation. {{first}} is the person's first name.
reactivate.confirm: Confirm button of the reactivate confirmation. {{first}} is the person's first name.
transfer.choose: Placeholder option of the new-owner select.
transfer.loadingPeople: Placeholder of the new-owner select while the list of people loads.
transfer.description: The dialog that hands what a person owns to another active person. {{first}} is the first name of the person it is taken from.
transfer.option: An option in the new-owner list: name and email.
transfer.whatMoved: Accessible name of the list of what moved, shown after the transfer.
transfer.nothingMoved: What moved of a kind, when nothing did.
transfer.failed: Error in the transfer dialog when handing what the person owns to someone else failed.
transfer.lost: Error in the transfer dialog when the connection failed during the transfer. {{why}} is the error message; {{first}} is the first name of the person it was taken from.
transfer.withApps: Before the data space's description, when apps move too: their data has to move with them.
transfer.title: The _done form is the title after the transfer, with the new owner's name.
transfer.nothing: Shown in the transfer dialog. {{first}} is the person's first name.
transfer.newOwner: Label of the select of the person who receives what is transferred.
transfer.nobodyActive: Shown in the transfer dialog when there is no other active person to choose.
transfer.whatMoves: Heading over the checkboxes of the kinds to transfer (apps, schedules, data…).
transfer.partialTitle: Bold start of a warning shown when only some kinds are ticked; transfer.partial follows.
transfer.partial: Warning when only some kinds are ticked. {{first}} is the first name of the person it is taken from.
transfer.transferring: Text of the confirm button while the transfer runs.
transfer.confirm: The confirm button with the new owner's first name; the _partial form when only some kinds are ticked.
transfer.pick: Confirm button of the transfer dialog before a new owner is chosen (disabled).
confirm.typeName: The admin types the person's name exactly, to confirm. Keep the <strong> tags around {{name}}.
confirm.nameField: Accessible name of the field where the admin types the person's name to confirm.
confirm.mismatch: Error under the name field when the typed name doesn't match.
confirm.waiting: While a new one-time confirmation (step-up challenge) is fetched from the server.
confirm.passwordForm: Accessible name of the form where the admin confirms with their own password.
confirm.password: Label of the admin's own password field in the confirmation.
confirm.startFailed: Error when the one-time confirmation (step-up challenge) can't be fetched from the server.
makeOwner.title: Hands the workspace ownership to another admin. The owner is the one admin others can't demote, deactivate or remove.
makeOwner.description: Body of the make-owner dialog. {{first}} is the first name of the admin who becomes the owner.
makeOwner.stepUp: Hint above the password field and passkey button: the admin confirms with their own password or passkey.
makeOwner.withPassword: Submit button of the password form. {{first}} is the new owner's first name.
makeOwner.withPasskey: Button that confirms with the admin's passkey instead. {{first}} is the new owner's first name.
makeOwner.withConfirm: The button on development servers, where no password or passkey is asked.
remove.planFailed: Error when the removal's dry run (the list of what would be deleted) can't be loaded.
remove.title: Removes a person permanently, after a backup: a dry run first, then a typed name and a password or passkey.
remove.description: Body of the remove dialog; the _done form after the removal succeeded.
remove.blocks: Heading of the list of reasons the removal can't go ahead yet.
remove.help.owned: Explains a reason the server gave for refusing the removal, in the admin's terms.
remove.records: A collapsed list of the database records the removal planner found for what they still own.
remove.transferFirst: Button under a blocking reason: opens the transfer dialog; the ellipsis says a dialog follows.
remove.deactivateFirst: Button under a blocking reason: opens the deactivate confirmation; the ellipsis says a dialog follows.
remove.goes: Heading of the list of what the removal deletes (database rows, files, stored objects).
remove.rowsAcross: Database rows, across how many tables.
remove.files: A count of files on the server's disk.
remove.objects: A count of objects in file storage.
remove.kept: Heading of the list of records the removal keeps, such as audit history.
remove.deleted: {{rows}} and {{tables}} are counted phrases ("12 rows", "3 tables").
remove.backup: Where the backup was written. <code/> is replaced by the backup's path; keep it.
remove.cleanupFailed: {{error}} is the server's error message. <code/> is replaced by a command to run on the server; keep it.
remove.cleaned: {{files}} and {{objects}} are counted phrases; {{size}} is their total size ("3.4 MB").
remove.stepUp: Hint above the password field and passkey button: the admin confirms with their own password or passkey.
remove.withPassword: Submit button of the password form. {{first}} is the person's first name.
remove.withPasskey: Button that confirms with the admin's passkey instead. {{first}} is the person's first name.
remove.withConfirm: The button on development servers, where no password or passkey is asked.
remove.back: Button after the removal: goes back to the list in Settings › People.
remove.continue: Button after the dry run: goes on to the confirm step (typed name and password or passkey).
